name: kubeflow-pipelines
description: End-to-end ML pipelines (train, tune, serve) with experiments and recurring runs.
overview:
**What it is** — Kubeflow Pipelines runs end-to-end ML pipelines (train, tune,
serve) with experiments and recurring runs. Kubernetes-native; deploys via
Flux from a Helm chart baked from kubeflow/manifests (multi-user
`platform-agnostic-multi-user`). For the supported browser UI, enable
**Kubeflow Platform** first so traffic goes through oauth2-proxy and the
dedicated Kubeflow gateway (Istio + Dex, not Traefik).

**Highlights**
- End-to-end pipelines (data → train → tune → serve)
- Experiments, recurring runs, and artifact tracking
- Tunable resources/replicas/scheduling via `configOverrides` (Helm-chart backed)

**Prerequisites**
- **Kubeflow Platform** (required) — enable it with `config.kubeflowIngressHost`
  before this app. Baked VirtualServices route `/pipeline/` through
  `oauth2-proxy`; without Platform there is no login path.
- **istio-helm** (required) — multi-user manifests include VirtualService,
  DestinationRule, and AuthorizationPolicy.
- **Namespace** — Deploys into the shared `kubeflow` namespace (upstream
  Pipelines hardcodes it). Platform also uses that namespace.

**How to use**

- **UI** — Open the Platform LoadBalancer URL at `/pipeline/` (same host as
  Central Dashboard at `/`). Do not port-forward `ml-pipeline-ui`: that
  skips oauth2-proxy, so the UI is missing `kubeflow-userid`.
- **API/SDK** — In-cluster HTTP API is `http://ml-pipeline.kubeflow.svc.cluster.local:8888`
  and is Istio-gated. Call it from a Profile namespace / authenticated
  workload, not from a raw port-forward. See
  [Connect the Pipelines SDK](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/user-guides/core-functions/connect-api/).

**Documentation:** [Kubeflow Pipelines](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/) | **Project:** [kubeflow/manifests](https://github.com/kubeflow/manifests)
